exceptions_and_traps.description: The verbs être, avoir, and savoir have irregular imperative forms that do not follow regular patterns.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Irregular imperative forms of être, avoir, savoir
grammar_rules.summary: être, avoir, and savoir have irregular imperative forms.
grammar_rules.explanation: The imperative forms of être, avoir, and savoir are irregular and must be memorized.
grammar_rules.formation: être: sois, soyons, soyez; avoir: aie, ayons, ayez; savoir: sache, sachons, sachez
restrictions: Applies only to être, avoir, and savoir
The tu form ends in -s (sois, aie, sache) instead of the regular -e
The forms cannot be derived from regular imperative endings and must be memorized
conditions: The verb is être, avoir, or savoir.
The imperative mood is used, with the irregular forms sois, aie, and sache.
exceptions: Only these three verbs are irregular in the imperative among the verbs taught here
The forms must be memorized and do not follow regular imperative endings
agreement_rules: Imperative forms agree with the addressee only: sois/soyez (être), aie/ayez (avoir), sache/sachez (savoir).
common_traps: Using regular endings for these irregular verbs.

stems.note: Irregular present: je sais, tu sais, il sait (attested).
nous savons, vous savez, ils savent (attested).
Irregular future stem, attested: je saurai; conditional je saurais.
Irregular subjunctive stem, attested: que je sache, que nous sachions; also the participle sachant.
Irregular past participle su (attested); the attested passé simple il sut / ils surent uses the same stem.

irregularities: Passé simple irrégulier sur le radical su-.
